name: bislerp resize
plain: Bilinear resampling where each 1D interpolation is a slerp of the channel vectors at a pixel rather than a lerp. It runs width first then height. Directions are slerped, magnitudes lerped, so per-pixel vector length is the lerped norm, which aims to avoid the contrast loss of plain bilinear.
math:
For neighbour pair (b1,b2) with ratio r, over channel dim:
u1=b1/‖b1‖, u2=b2/‖b2‖ (zero norm→0), dot=u1·u2, ω=acos(dot)
res = [sin((1−r)ω)/sin ω]·u1 + [sin(rω)/sin ω]·u2
res *= ‖b1‖(1−r) + ‖b2‖r
if dot>1−1e−5 res=b1 (ignores r); if dot<−1+1e−5 res=lerp
ratios and indices come from interpolating a coordinate ramp with torch bilinear (align_corners false).
